zh: 一个国家可能孕育出自己的蛮族入侵者。
en: A nation may beget its own barbarian invaders.

zh: ——威廉·勒普克（Röpke），1942年
en: —Wilhelm Röpke, 1942

zh: 到二十世纪末，人们普遍认为自由市场意识形态已经征服了世界。在全球经济的推拉起伏之中，国家的重要性正在退潮。1995年，美国总统比尔·克林顿在这个时代的一处标志性场所——达沃斯世界经济论坛——上指出：“24小时运转的市场能以令人目眩的速度作出反应，有时甚至冷酷无情。”
德国总理格哈德·施罗德宣布对两德统一后的福利制度进行重大改革时，援引了“全球化的风暴”。他说，社会市场经济必须实现现代化，否则就将“被不受约束的市场力量所现代化”。
政治已经变成了被动语态。唯一的行动者是全球经济。美联储主席艾伦·格林斯潘在2007年把这一点说得最为直白，他宣称：“下一任总统是谁几乎毫无关系。世界是由市场力量治理的。”
在批评者看来，这像一个新帝国，其中“全球化正在取代殖民主义”。
而在它的拥护者看来，这是一个商品和资本按供需逻辑流动的世界，人员则未必如此；这种流动为所有人创造繁荣，或至少创造机会。
这种市场力量统治的哲学被批评者贴上了“新自由主义”的标签。我们被告知，新自由主义者信奉全球范围的自由放任：自我调节的市场、缩小的国家，并把人类的一切动机还原为经济人（Homo economicus）那一维的理性自利。据说，新自由主义的全球主义者们把自由市场资本主义与民主混为一谈，并幻想着一个没有边界的单一世界市场。
en: By the end of the twentieth century it was a common belief that free-market ideology had conquered the world. The importance of states was receding in the push and pull of the global economy. At the World Economic Forum at Davos in 1995, an iconic location of the era, U.S. president Bill Clinton observed that “24-hour markets can respond with blinding speed and sometimes ruthlessness.”

Chancellor Gerhard Schröder referenced the “storms of globalization” as he announced a major reform of the welfare system in reunified Germany. The social market economy, he said, must modernize or it would “be modernized by the unchecked forces of the market.”

Politics had moved to the passive tense. The only actor was the global economy. U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan put the point most bluntly in 2007 when he declared, “It hardly makes any difference who will be the next president. The world is governed by market forces.”
To its critics, this looked like a new empire with “globalization substituting for colonialism.”
To its champions, it was a world in which goods and capital, if not people, flowed according to the logic of supply and demand, creating prosperity—or at least opportunity—for all.

This philosophy of the rule of market forces was labeled “neoliberalism” by its critics. Neoliberals, we were told, believed in global laissez-faire: self-regulating markets, shrunken states, and the reduction of all human motivation to the one-dimensional rational self-interest of
The neoliberal globalists, it was claimed, conflated free-market capitalism with democracy and fantasized about a single world market without borders.

zh: 我的叙事要对这一流行说法加以纠正。本书表明，自称新自由主义者的人们并不相信市场作为自主实体能够自我调节。他们并不认为民主与资本主义是同义词。他们并不认为人只受经济理性驱动。他们既不追求国家的消失，也不追求边界的消失。他们也不仅仅透过个体的透镜来看待世界。事实上，新自由主义奠基性的洞见可与约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯和卡尔·波兰尼的洞见相比拟：市场不会、也不能照管自己。二十世纪新自由主义理论思考的核心，在于他们所称的、在整个世界尺度上保卫资本主义所必需的“元经济的”（meta-economic）或“超经济的”（extra-economic）条件。我要表明，新自由主义规划的重点在于设计制度——不是为了解放市场，而是为了围封（encase）市场，使资本主义对民主的威胁产生免疫，创建一个框架以约束常常是非理性的人类行为，并在帝国之后把世界重新安排为一个由相互竞争的国家构成的空间，其中边界履行着一种必要的功能。
en: My narrative corrects this storyline. It shows that self-described neoliberals did not believe in self-regulating markets as autonomous entities. They did not see democracy and capitalism as synonymous. They did not see humans as motivated only by economic rationality. They sought neither the disappearance of the state nor the disappearance of borders. And they did not see the world only through the lens of the individual. In fact, the foundational neoliberal insight is comparable to that of John Maynard Keynes and Karl Polanyi: the market does not and cannot take care of itself. The core of twentieth-century neoliberal theorizing involves what they called the meta-economic or extra-economic conditions for safeguarding capitalism at the scale of the entire world. I show that the neoliberal project focused on designing institutions—not to liberate markets but to encase them, to inoculate capitalism against the threat of democracy, to create a framework to contain often-irrational human behavior, and to reorder the world after empire as a space of competing states in which borders fulfill a necessary function.

zh: 我们如何理解新自由主义——我们甚至能否使用这个名称？多年来，许多人声称这个词几乎毫无意义。一位学者最近声称，“就一切实际意义而言，根本不存在”所谓新自由主义理论。
然而在2016年，国际货币基金组织（International Monetary Fund，IMF）登上国际头条：它不仅将新自由主义认定为一种融贯的学说，还追问私有化、放松管制与自由化这一揽子政策是否被“过度推销”了。
《财富》（
）杂志当时报道称：“就连国际货币基金组织如今也承认新自由主义已经失败。”
该杂志暗示这是一种新动向，则多少有些不准确。与新自由主义相关的政策——至少在言辞上——受到挑战已有二十年之久。较早的怀疑表态出现在1997年亚洲金融危机之后的约瑟夫·斯蒂格利茨身上。
斯蒂格利茨于1997年至2000年担任世界银行首席经济学家，并获诺贝尔经济学奖，他成了新自由主义全球化的直言不讳的批评者。1990年代末，其他批评者宣称，不受监管的全球自由市场是“最后的乌托邦”——国际金融机构也部分地表示认同。
它们放弃了教条式的资本管制反对立场，而资本管制恰恰是2016年那篇《财富》文章的主题。世界贸易组织（World Trade Organization，WTO）也以类似方式改变了自己的形象。在抗议活动迫使其中断1999年的会议之后，该组织转向强调全球化的人类面向。
en: How can we make sense of neoliberalism—and can we even use that name? For years many have claimed that the term is virtually meaningless. “There is for all practical purposes, no such thing” as neoliberal theory, one scholar claimed recently.

In 2016, however, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), making international headlines, not only identified neoliberalism as a coherent doctrine but asked if the policy package of privatization, deregulation, and liberalization had been “oversold.”
reported at the time that “even the IMF now admits neoliberalism has failed.”

The magazine’s suggestion that this was a new development was somewhat inaccurate. The policies associated with neoliberalism had been challenged—at least rhetorically—for two decades. An early expression of doubt came from Joseph Stiglitz after the Asian financial crisis of 1997.

World Bank chief economist from 1997 to 2000 and winner of the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics, Stiglitz became a vocal critic of neoliberal globalization. In the late 1990s other critics declared that the unregulated global free market was “the last utopia”—and the international financial institutions partly agreed.
They dropped their doctrinaire opposition to capital controls, the very subject of the 2016
article. The World Trade Organization (WTO) underwent a similar facelift. After protests shut down its 1999 meeting, it pivoted to emphasize the human side of globalization.

zh: 尽管那些被称作新自由主义的政策早已受到批评，国际货币基金组织的报告仍因承认“新自由主义”这个标签而意义重大。这个词看似已准备进入主流，出现在《金融时报》（Financial Times）、《卫报》（Guardian）和其他报纸上。
同样是在2016年，成立于1977年、曾为玛格丽特·撒切尔提供政策指引的亚当·斯密研究所，用他们自己的话说“公开宣称自己是新自由主义者”，抛弃了从前的名号“自由至上主义者”（libertarian）。
“世界观上是全球主义者”是他们为自己标榜的原则之一。2017年，德国瓦尔特·欧肯研究所的所长公开为他所谓的“经典新自由主义”辩护，捍卫其建立“一个凌驾于各游说集团利益之上的强大国家”的主张。
看来，对批评者和支持者双方而言，那个“不敢说出自己名字的运动”如今终于可以名其名之了。
这是一种澄清性的发展。为新自由主义命名，有助于我们把新自由主义看作众多思想体系之一和众多治理方式之一——作为一种规制形式或规制变体，而非规制的激进他者。
en: Even though the policies described as neoliberal had long been criticized, the IMF report was still significant for recognizing the label “neoliberalism.” The term appeared poised for the mainstream, appearing in the
the
and other newspapers.
Also in 2016, the Adam Smith Institute, founded in 1977 and a source of guidance for Margaret Thatcher, “came out as neoliberals,” in their words, shedding their former moniker, “libertarian.”

“Globalist in outlook” was one of the principles they claimed for themselves. In 2017 the director of the Walter Eucken Institute in Germany publicly defended the honor of what he called “classic neoliberalism” and its call for “a strong state standing above the interests of lobbies.”
It seemed that for both critics and proponents “the movement that dared not speak its own name” could now be named.

This was a clarifying development. Labeling neoliberalism helps us to see it as one body of thought and one mode of governance among others—as a form or variety of regulation rather than its radical Other.

zh: 在过去十年里，人们付出了非凡的努力，把新自由主义及其全球治理处方历史化，把这一“政治骂词”或“反自由派口号”变成严谨档案研究的对象。
我的叙事将两股长久以来出奇地互不往来的学术脉络编织在一起。第一股脉络是追溯新自由主义运动思想史的工作。
第二股脉络是社会科学家——而非历史学家——对新自由主义全球主义理论的研究。学者们已经表明，“新自由主义”一词最早造于1938年巴黎的沃尔特·李普曼座谈会（Walter Lippmann Colloquium），用以描述与会经济学家、社会学家、记者和商界领袖想要“革新”自由主义的愿望。
正如一位学者所论证的，研究新自由主义最站得住脚的方式之一，是把它看作“一个在共同思想框架内交换意见的有组织的个人群体”。
历史学家尤其关注朝圣山学社（Mont Pèlerin Society，1947年由F. A. 哈耶克等人创立），把它看作一群志同道合的知识分子和政策制定者，定期聚会讨论世界事务，以及他们所致力的政治事业在当下的境况。正如上述论著所示，这个群体并非没有内部裂痕。不过，除货币政策与发展经济学之外，国际治理与全球治理问题在这些历史叙述中出人意料地遭到忽视。
尽管这些思想家之间存在分歧，我的论点是：我们能够在他们的著述与行动中辨识出一套融贯的世界秩序处方的粗略轮廓。他们将秩序自由主义（ordoliberalism）“以秩序思考”的原则全球化，其以世界秩序思考的规划提出了一整套方案，旨在保卫世界经济，使之免受那种直到二十世纪才扩展到全球的民主所带来的冲击。民主的全球扩展带来了古典自由主义者这些先驱不可能预见的局面和挑战。
en: In the last decade, extraordinary efforts have been made to historicize neoliberalism and its prescriptions for global governance, and to transform the “political swearword” or “anti-liberal slogan” into a subject of rigorous archival research.
My narrative knits together two strands of scholarship that have remained strangely disconnected. The first strand is the work to trace the intellectual history of the neoliberal movement.

The second strand is the study of neoliberal globalist theory by social scientists, not historians. Scholars have shown that the term “neoliberalism” was coined first at the Walter Lippmann Colloquium in Paris in 1938 as a way to describe the desire of the gathered economists, sociologists, journalists, and business leaders to “renovate” liberalism.
As one scholar argues, one of the most defensible ways to study neoliberalism is as “an organized group of individuals exchanging ideas within a common intellectual framework.”

Historians have focused, in particular, on the Mont Pèlerin Society, formed by F. A. Hayek and others in 1947, as a group of like-minded intellectuals and policy makers who would meet periodically to discuss world affairs and the contemporary condition of the political cause to which they were devoted. This group was not without its internal rifts, as the works cited have shown. Apart from monetary policy and development economics, though, the question of international and global governance has been surprisingly neglected in these histories.

Although there were differences among these thinkers, my contention is that we can discern the broad strokes of a coherent prescription for world order in their writings and actions. Globalizing the ordoliberal principle of “thinking in orders,” their project of thinking in world orders offered a set of proposals designed to defend the world economy from a democracy that became global only in the twentieth century—producing a state of affairs and a set of challenges that their predecessors, the classical liberals, could never have predicted.

zh: 对塑造全球秩序的新自由主义理念最具洞察力的研究者，不是历史学家而是社会科学家。在过去二十年里，政治学家和社会学家发展出一套针对新自由主义规划的缜密分析。他们辨识出将市场行动者隔绝于民主压力之外的种种努力，其载体涵盖一系列机构——从国际货币基金组织和世界银行，到世界各地的港口管理机构和中央银行（包括欧洲中央银行）、像欧洲联盟这样的治理结构、像《北美自由贸易协定》（NAFTA）这样的贸易条约，以及世界贸易组织。他们还在国际投资法的扩张中看到了这种隔绝努力：国际投资法旨在保护外国投资者免于各种形式的征收，并提供一套平行的全球法律体系，即所谓跨国商法（transnational law merchant）。
他们追溯了避税天堂构成的“离岸世界”的出现与各类特区的激增——这一切都是为资本提供安全港，使其不必担心累进税或再分配政策的侵犯。
把新自由主义理解为一种特定的制度建设规划，而非含混的“逻辑”或“理性”时，“隔绝市场”是描述其目标的恰当比喻。社会科学家在界定这种隔绝方面的工作是严谨的，但他们对新自由主义理论史的把握却相形见绌——他们往往只给哈耶克、米尔顿·弗里德曼这样的知识分子安排过场角色。
人们说，这些新自由主义名家的思想启发或“提示”了某些全球和区域的治理形式，却留下疑问让我们琢磨：这种影响究竟是如何发生的，这些思想最初又是从何而来。尤其是哈耶克这个名字，往往充当一个自由漂浮的能指，而非指向一个真实历史人物的索引。例如，有人把欧盟称作“哈耶克式联邦”，也有人把“离开”（
）欧盟的意愿称为“重振哈耶克之梦”的希望。
哈耶克这样的思想家究竟期许的是什么？新自由主义全球主义的思想于何时何地起源？我把新自由主义全球主义思想的一个关键起源点，定位在帝国终结之际发生的划时代秩序转变之中。我认为，非殖民化对于新自由主义世界治理模式的出现居于核心地位。
en: The clearest-eyed academic observers of the neoliberal philosophy of global ordering have been not historians but social scientists. For the last twenty years, political scientists and sociologists have elaborated a sophisticated analysis of the neoliberal project. They have identified efforts to insulate market actors from democratic pressures in a series of institutions from the IMF and the World Bank to port authorities and central banks worldwide, including the European Central Bank, governance structures like the European Union, trade treaties like the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), and the WTO. They have also seen efforts to insulate in the expansion of international investment law designed to protect foreign investors from diverse forms of expropriation and to provide a parallel global legal system known as the transnational law merchant.

They have traced the emergence of an “offshore world” of tax havens and the proliferation of zones of many types, all designed to provide safe harbor for capital, free from fear of infringement by policies of progressive taxation or redistribution.

“Insulation of markets” is a useful metaphorical description of the aim of neoliberalism as a specific institution-building project rather than as a nebulous “logic” or “rationality.” The work of social scientists in defining this insulation has been rigorous, but their history of neoliberal theory has been less so—they often give intellectuals such as Hayek and Milton Friedman only walk-on roles.

The ideas of such neoliberal luminaries are said to inspire or “suggest” certain forms of global and regional governance, yet we are left to wonder how this influence actually happened and where the ideas came from in the first place. The name of Hayek, in particular, often operates as a free-floating signifier more than an index to an actual historical figure. Some label the European Union a “Hayekian federation,” for example, while others call the desire to
the EU a hope of “reviving Hayek’s dream.”

What exactly did thinkers like Hayek wish for, and where and when did the ideas of neoliberal globalism originate? I locate a key point of origin of neoliberal globalist thinking within the epochal shift of order that occurred at the end of empire. Decolonization, I argue, was central to the emergence of the neoliberal model of world governance.

zh: 是围封，不是解放
要按新自由主义者自己的说法来理解他们，障碍之一便是过度依赖从匈牙利经济史家卡尔·波兰尼那里借来的一套观念。正如一位学者指出的，波兰尼已成为“继米歇尔·福柯之后，大概也是当今社会科学家中最受欢迎的理论家”。
在许多解释新自由主义全球化的尝试中，波兰尼1944年的著作《大转型》（

）的回溯性影响十分显著。按照那些改写波兰尼叙事的人的说法，新自由主义者的“市场原教旨主义”促使他们试图将“自然的”市场从社会中“脱嵌”，从而实现其“自我调节的市场”的乌托邦梦想。人们通常都会指出，波兰尼实际写的是十九世纪；但批评者往往径直断言，波兰尼已经预先批判了新自由主义。与波兰尼式语言一脉相承的，是这样一种观念：新自由主义者的目标在于解放市场或让市场自由。“unfettered”（不受束缚的）这个本身并不常见的形容词，被习惯性地接在“市场”之上，既作为新自由主义的目标，也作为其假定的现实。
尽管并非新自由主义理论诸作者的本意，这个隐喻却把批判对象本质化了：市场变成了一个能够被行动者解放的东西，而不是像新自由主义者自己所相信的那样，是一套依赖制度框架的关系。
en: One of the obstacles to understanding neoliberals on their own terms has been an excessive reliance on a set of ideas borrowed from the Hungarian economic historian Karl Polanyi, who has become, as one scholar notes, “after Michel Foucault, probably the most popular theorist among social scientists today.”
Across many attempts to account for neoliberal globalization, the retroactive influence of Polanyi’s 1944 book

is marked. According to those who adapt Polanyi’s narrative, the “market fundamentalism” of neoliberals led them to seek to “disembed” the “natural” market from society and thus realize their utopian dream of a “self-regulating market.” It is noted routinely that Polanyi was actually writing about the nineteenth century, but critics often make the leap to say that this was a critique of neoliberalism before the fact. Of a piece with the Polanyian language is the idea that the goal of neoliberals is to liberate markets or set them free. The otherwise uncommon adjective “unfettered” is attached habitually to “markets” as both neoliberal goal and putative reality.

Against the intention of the authors of neoliberal theory, this metaphor essential-izes the object of critique: the market becomes a thing capable of being liberated by agents, instead of being, as neoliberals themselves believed, a set of relationships that rely on an institutional framework.

zh: 对波兰尼诸范畴的运用带来了关键洞见，我也承接千禧年以来学者们的努力，把新自由主义规划构想为国家职能“同时收缩与扩张”（a simultaneous roll-back
of state functions）的过程。
改造波兰尼的概念，有学者甚至写下了“嵌入型新自由主义”。

然而，如果我们想按新自由主义自身的术语来理解其思想——这是批判必不可少的第一步——就不应被那种摆脱国家而获得自由的自我调节市场的观念所误导。浏览那些关心全球秩序的新自由主义者的著述，人们会发现一个事实的重要性：波兰尼是他们的同时代人。和他一样，他们认为大萧条证明旧式资本主义已难以为继，于是着手为资本主义生存所需的更广泛条件建立理论。用一位学者的话说，哈耶克和波兰尼都“关心针对自由市场的社会—制度回应”。
事实上，哈耶克发展了他自己的“作为社会嵌入之物的自由市场”的观念。
如果我们过分强调市场原教旨主义这个范畴，就会忽略一点：新自由主义方案的真正焦点不是市场本身，而是重新设计国家、法律及其他制度以保护市场。法学研究者对世界贸易日益加深的“法律化”或“司法化”已有明确的论述。
聚焦哈耶克及其合作者，使我们能够在新自由主义思想史的脉络内部理解这一趋势。
en: The applications of Polanyi’s categories have led to key insights, and I build on the efforts of scholars since the turn of the millennium to conceive of the neoliberal project as “a simultaneous roll-back
of state functions.”
Adapting Polanyi, some scholars have even written of “embedded neoliberalism.”

Yet if we want to understand neoliberal thought on its own terms—an essential first step of critique—we should not be misled by the notion of a self-regulating market liberated from the state. Looking at the writings of the neoliberals concerned with global order, one discovers the importance of the fact that Polanyi was their contemporary. Like him, they saw the Great Depression as evidence that the old form of capitalism was unworkable, and they set about theorizing the broader conditions required for its survival. In the words of one scholar, both Hayek and Polanyi were “concerned with socio-institutional responses to the free market.”
In fact, Hayek developed his own idea of “free markets as socially embedded.”

If we place too much emphasis on the category of market fundamentalism, we will fail to notice that the real focus of neoliberal proposals is not on the market per se but on redesigning states, laws, and other institutions to protect the market. Legal scholars have been clear on the increasing “legalization” or “juridicization” of world trade.
Focusing on Hayek and his collaborators allows us to understand this within the intellectual history of neoliberal thought.

zh: 2006年，一篇刊于重要新自由主义期刊《秩序》（
）上的文章澄清说，新自由主义运动的创始人之所以“加上了‘neo’（新）这个音节”，是因为他们认识到需要“以更明确、也不同于以往的方式确立国家的角色”，其中包括更多关注“法律—制度框架”。
新自由主义者绝非怀有市场能脱离人为干预而自行运作的乌托邦信念；恰恰相反，“新自由主义者……指出的是一个自由经济体系的超经济条件”。
有一个事实未获充分承认：德国秩序自由主义和奥地利学派的焦点都不是经济本身，而是为经济开辟空间的制度。
当哈耶克谈到“经济的自我调节力量”时——例如他在弗莱堡履新的就职演说中便曾如此——他紧接着就讨论了经济需要一个“框架”的问题。
他的工作主要围绕一个问题展开，即如何设计他在《通往奴役之路》（The Road to Serfdom）之后所出的下一本书中所说的“自由宪章”（constitution of liberty）。
en: A 2006 article in the leading neoliberal journal

clarified that the founders of the neoliberal movement “added the syllable ‘neo’ ” because they recognized the need to establish “the role of the state both more clearly and differently,” including increased attention to the “legal-institutional framework.”
Far from having a utopian belief in the market as operating independently of human intervention, “neoliberals … have pointed to the extra-economic conditions for a free economic system.”
It is an inadequately acknowledged fact that the focus of both German ordoliberalism and Austrian economics is not on the economy as such but on the institutions creating a space for the economy.

When Hayek referred to the “self-regulating forces of the economy”—as he did, for example, in his inaugural lecture when taking up his position in Freiburg—he followed immediately with a discussion of the need for a “framework” for the economy.
The overwhelming focus of his work was on the problem of designing what he called, in his next book after
a “constitution of liberty.”

zh: 一位学者写道：“哈耶克清楚地看到，市场是一种社会制度，它嵌入于使它能够获得意义的形形色色的制度之中。”
哈耶克本人驳斥了他呼吁建立“最小国家”的说法。
尽管“强国家与自由市场”这个简称在解释新自由主义时有其用处，但如何定义“强”却并非不言自明。
有学者提出，从数量而非质量的意义上思考国家几乎没有意义；应把需要“多少”国家的问题替换为需要“什么样”的国家的问题。
后面的各章将按时间顺序阐发这样一个新自由主义观念：市场不是自然的，而是为围封市场而以政治手段建构制度的产物。市场支撑着文化价值的库藏，而这些文化价值是市场持续存在的必要但不充分条件。
en: “Hayek saw clearly,” one scholar writes, “that the market is a social institution embedded in a great variety of institutions in which it gains meaning.”
Hayek himself dismissed the idea that he was calling for a “minimal state.”
Although the shorthand phrase “strong state and free market” has its usefulness in explaining neoliberalism, how one defines strength is not self-evident.
One scholar has argued that it makes little sense to think of the state in quantitative rather than qualitative terms; the question of “how much” state should be replaced by “what kind” of state.

The chapters that follow provide an exposition through time of the neoliberal idea that markets are not natural but are products of the political construction of institutions to encase them. Markets buttress the repository of cultural values that are a necessary but not sufficient condition for markets’ continued existence.

zh: 是日内瓦学派，不是芝加哥学派

1983年，哈耶克的一位学生、顶尖的国际经济法学家恩斯特-乌尔里希·彼得斯曼写道：“新自由主义经济理论的共同出发点是这样一个洞见：在任何运转良好的市场经济中，市场竞争的‘看不见的手’都必然要由法律的‘看得见的手’加以补充。”他列举了众所周知的各新自由主义思想学派：作为德国秩序自由主义诞生地、瓦尔特·欧肯与弗朗茨·伯姆执教于斯的弗莱堡学派；与米尔顿·弗里德曼、亚伦·迪雷克特、理查德·波斯纳等人联系在一起的芝加哥学派；以及路德维希·米勒-阿尔马克的科隆学派。然后，他提到了一个几乎默默无闻的学派：日内瓦学派（Geneva School）。
en: In 1983 one of Hayek’s students, the leading international economic lawyer Ernst-Ulrich Petersmann, wrote, “The common starting point of the neoliberal economic theory is the insight that in any well-functioning market economy the ‘invisible hand’ of market competition must by necessity be complemented by the ‘visible hand’ of the law.” He listed the well-known neoliberal schools of thought: the Freiburg School, birthplace of German ordoliberalism, and home to Walter Eucken and Franz Böhm; the Chicago School, identified with Milton Friedman, Aaron Director, Richard Posner, and others; and the Cologne School of Ludwig Müller-Armack. Then he cited a virtual unknown: the Geneva School.

zh: 谁是日内瓦学派？或者说，日内瓦学派是什么？后面的各章将叙述一支被历史学家忽视的新自由主义流派。我介绍的一组思想家尚未成为英语文献中的核心人物，而哈耶克这样早已居于核心的人物，我也将重新加以定位。我沿用并扩展“日内瓦学派”这个标签，用以描述一个新自由主义思想的族类，它从十九世纪末（fin-de-siècle）维也纳的研讨室，一直延伸到千禧年之交（fin-de-millennium）日内瓦的世界贸易组织大厦。我引入这个术语，既不是为了招致围绕谁可入选的吹毛求疵，也不是为了对其成员名单争执不休。毋宁说，我的意图是补救把形形色色的思想家统统纳入“新自由主义者”这一个伞式术语所造成的混乱。日内瓦学派为与新自由主义思想中世界秩序相关、却或多或少隐没在暗处的那些层面，提供了初步而有益的阐明。如本书所提议的，日内瓦学派包括：在瑞士日内瓦担任学术职位的思想家，其中有威廉·勒普克（Röpke）、路德维希·冯·米塞斯、迈克尔·海尔佩林；在日内瓦从事或发表关键研究的人，包括哈耶克、莱昂内尔·罗宾斯、戈特弗里德·哈伯勒；以及在关税与贸易总协定（General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade，GATT，即关贸总协定）工作过的人，如扬·图姆利尔、弗里德·勒斯勒尔与彼得斯曼本人。尽管与弗莱堡学派有相通之处，日内瓦学派的新自由主义者仍将秩序自由主义“经济宪法”（economic constitution）——即支配经济生活之规则的总体——的观念移调到了民族国家之外的尺度。
en: Who or what was the Geneva School? The following chapters present a narrative about a strain of neoliberalism that has been neglected by historians. I introduce a set of thinkers who have not been central in the English literature and reframe those like Hayek who have been. I adopt and expand the label “Geneva School” to describe a genus of neoliberal thought that stretches from the seminar rooms of fin-de-siècle Vienna to the halls of the WTO in fin-de-millennium Geneva. My goal in introducing the term is neither to invite hairsplitting about inclusion nor to litigate the roster of its members. Rather, my intention is to remedy the confusion produced when diverse thinkers are contained under the single umbrella term “neoliberal.” The Geneva School offers provisional but helpful illumination of those aspects of neoliberal thought related to world order that have remained more or less in the shadows. As proposed here, the Geneva School includes thinkers who held academic positions in Geneva, Switzerland, among them Wilhelm Röpke, Ludwig von Mises, and Michael Heilperin; those who pursued or presented key research there, including Hayek, Lionel Robbins, and Gottfried Haberler; and those who worked at the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), such as Jan Tumlir, Frieder Roessler, and Petersmann himself. Although they shared affinities with the Freiburg School, Geneva School neoliberals transposed the ordoliberal idea of “the economic constitution”—or the totality of rules governing economic life—to the scale beyond the nation.

zh: 日内瓦学派对新自由主义思想的独特贡献，在英语讨论中常常遭到忽视。新自由主义运动的大多数历史，都从1930年代和1940年代欧洲大陆的聚会讲起，随后便把目光转向美国和英国，叙述里根与撒切尔在1980年代实现新自由主义突破前的情形。这一转向伴随着对芝加哥学派——尤其是弗里德曼——的刻意聚焦。尽管法律与经济学领域，以及詹姆斯·M. 布坎南和弗吉尼亚学派其他人的公共选择理论，如今也受到一些令人欢迎的关注，总体趋势仍是偏向从英美一侧来理解新自由主义思想。
这样做的缺失在于：那些留在欧洲大陆的人、或像哈耶克那样回到欧洲的人，其贡献的重要性被漏掉了。纠正这一遗漏至关重要，因为正是欧洲的新自由主义者最关注国际秩序问题。
en: The distinct contributions of the Geneva School to neoliberal thought are often neglected in English-language discussions. Most histories of the neoliberal movement begin in continental Europe with the meetings in the 1930s and 1940s but shift their gaze to the United States and Great Britain ahead of the neoliberal breakthrough of Reagan and Thatcher in the 1980s. This shift is accompanied by a pointed focus on the Chicago School, and Friedman in particular. Even though some welcome attention is now being given to the field of law and economics and the public choice theory of James M. Buchanan and others of the Virginia School, the overall tendency has been toward an understanding of neoliberal thought that tilts toward the Anglo-American side.

What this misses is the importance of the contributions of those who remained in continental Europe or who, like Hayek, returned to Europe. Correcting this elision is critical because it was the European neoliberals who were most attentive to questions of international order.

zh: 我的叙事呈现的是从中欧眺望的新自由主义全球主义愿景，因为最一贯地把世界视为整体来观察的，正是中欧的新自由主义者。芝加哥学派和弗吉尼亚学派的思想家都表现出一种美国特有的品质：无视世界的其余部分，同时又假定美国是世界的行之有效的范例。

欧洲的新自由主义者没有这份奢侈，因为在二十世纪的大部分时间里，他们生活在程度不等的美国霸权影响之下。中欧的新自由主义者成为世界秩序的早熟理论家，顺理成章。他们的国家没有美国那样广阔的国内市场，因此不得不更加关注通过贸易或兼并进入世界市场的问题。第一次世界大战后帝国在中欧的及早终结，也要求他们思考平衡国家权力与经济相互依存的策略。尽管故事始于维也纳，但这座位于瑞士湖边的城市——日内瓦，最终的世界贸易组织总部所在地——成了那群寻求解开帝国之后秩序之谜的思想家的精神首都。
en: My narrative presents a vision of neoliberal globalism viewed from Central Europe, because it was Central European neoliberals who most consistently looked at the world as a whole. Both Chicago School and Virginia School thinkers exhibited the peculiarly American quality of ignoring the rest of the world while assuming that America was a working model of it.

European neoliberals did not have this luxury, as they existed for most of the century under the influence of varying levels of U.S. hegemony. It made sense that Central European neoliberals were precocious theorists of world order. Their countries did not enjoy a vast domestic market like that of the United States, so they were forced to be more attentive to the question of access to the world market through either trade or annexation. The early end of empire in Central Europe after the First World War also required them to contemplate strategies for balancing state power with economic interdependence. Although the story begins in Vienna, the Swiss city on the lake, Geneva—eventually the home of the WTO—became the spiritual capital of the group of thinkers who sought to solve the riddle of postimperial order.

zh: 多数历史学家会主张，世界秩序问题在二十世纪早期就已大体尘埃落定，胜出的是弗拉基米尔·列宁和伍德罗·威尔逊同时提出、并得到全世界反殖民行动者要求的民族自决（self-determination）理念。在这种看法中，自决原则在凡尔赛受挫——因为美国和欧洲帝国不愿践行自己的口号——又遭到意大利和德国法西斯扩张主义的阻截，后来还受制于苏联对其卫星国的控制，最终随着第二次世界大战后的非殖民化浪潮取得胜利，最近则体现在南非种族隔离的终结与苏联在东欧统治的落幕上。日内瓦学派的新自由主义者不同意这一叙事。在他们看来，若把对民族主权与自主的承诺当真，那是危险的。他们是民族主权的坚定批评者，相信帝国之后，各民族国家必须继续嵌入一套国际制度秩序，以保卫资本并保护资本在全世界流动的权利。二十世纪的首要罪过，是对不受约束的民族独立的信仰；而新自由主义的世界秩序要求可执行的“同法”（isonomy）——哈耶克后来称之为“同样的法”（same law）——以对抗“自主”（autonomy）即“自己的法”（own law）的幻觉。
en: Most historians would claim that the question of world order had been more or less settled early in the century in favor of the idea of national self-determination offered by both Vladimir Lenin and Woodrow Wilson and demanded by anticolonial actors worldwide. In that view, the principle of self-determination, thwarted at Versailles by the unwillingness of the United States and European empires to live up to their own rhetoric, and waylaid by the fascist expansionism of Italy and Germany and later the Soviet control over its satellite states, eventually triumphed with the wave of decolonization after the Second World War and, most recently, with the end of apartheid in South Africa and Soviet rule in Eastern Europe. Geneva School neoliberals disagreed with this narrative. To their mind, commitments to national sovereignty and autonomy were dangerous if taken seriously. They were stalwart critics of national sovereignty, believing that after empire, nations must remain embedded in an international institutional order that safeguarded capital and protected its right to move throughout the world. The cardinal sin of the twentieth century was the belief in unfettered national independence, and the neoliberal world order required enforceable isonomy—or “same law,” as Hayek would later call it—against the illusion of autonomy, or “own law.”

zh: 日内瓦学派的新自由主义者以其独特的地理观，调和了世界经济与民族国家世界之间的张力。他们的全球想象由曾为纳粹法学家的卡尔·施米特在1950年勾勒出来。施米特提出，世界不是一个，而是两个。一个是划分为有边界的领土国家的世界，政府在其中统治着人。他用罗马法术语把这称为统治权（imperium）的世界。另一个是财产的世界，人们在其中拥有散布于地球各地的事物、货币和土地。这就是所有权（dominium）的世界。现代资本主义的这种双重世界在十九世纪成形。外国投资的无处不在，使人们在并非其公民、甚至从未踏足的国家拥有企业的全部或部分成为家常便饭。货币几乎在任何地方都通行，并能按金本位制的固定汇率兑换成主要货币或兑回。合同由成文与不成文的商业行为准则普遍保障执行。甚至连军事占领也不影响私人财产。与早期的劫掠时代不同，敌军席卷而去之后，土地或企业仍然属于你。在施米特看来，所有权与统治权之间的划分，比国外与国内这种纯粹政治的区分更为根本。最重要的边界并不像切橙子那样把世界一分为二——东方与西方，或北方与南方——而是像橙子的白瓤与外皮那样，让彼此重叠的两个整体各自保持完整。他写道：“在那些看起来纯粹政治的国家间国际法的国家—政治边界的上面、下面和旁边，弥漫着一个自由的、亦即非国家的经济领域，渗透一切：一个全球经济。”
en: Geneva School neoliberals reconciled the tension between the world economy and the world of nations through their own distinct geography. Their global imaginary was sketched by the erstwhile Nazi jurist Carl Schmitt in 1950. Schmitt proposed that there was not one world but two. One was the world partitioned into bounded, territorial states where governments ruled over human beings. This he called the world of
using the Roman legal term. The other was the world of property, where people owned things, money, and land scattered across the earth. This was the world of

The doubled world of modern capitalism coalesced in the nineteenth century. The ubiquity of foreign investment had made it routine for people to own all or part of enterprises in countries where they were not citizens and had never even set foot. Money worked almost anywhere and could be exchanged into and out of major currencies at the fixed rates of the gold standard. Contracts were enforced universally by written and unwritten codes of business conduct. Even military occupation did not affect private property. Unlike earlier eras of plunder, the land or business was still yours after the enemy army had swept through. To Schmitt, the division between dominium and imperium was more fundamental than the purely political distinction of foreign and domestic. The most important border did not halve the world like an orange into East and West, or North and South, but preserved overlapping wholes in suspension, like an orange’s pith and peel. “Over, under and beside the state-political borders of what appeared to be a purely political international law between states,” he wrote, “spread a free, i.e. non-state sphere of economy permeating everything: a global economy.”

zh: 施米特说这一双重世界，本意是负面的：它妨碍国家主权的充分行使。但新自由主义者却觉得，他对他们想要维护（con-serve）的世界给出了最佳描述。在日内瓦任教近三十年的威廉·勒普克相信，恰恰是这一划分将成为自由世界秩序的基础。理想的新自由主义秩序将通过可执行的世界法来维持两个全球领域之间的平衡，创造“最小限度的宪政秩序”和“国家—公共领域与私人领域的分离”。
在1955年于海牙国际法学院发表的演讲中，勒普克强调了这一划分的重要性，同时指出了它的悖论。“裁抑民族主权，确确实实是我们时代最迫切的需要之一，”他论述道，但“主权的过剩应当被废除，而不是转移到更高的政治与地理单位去”。
en: Schmitt meant the doubled world as something negative, an impingement on the full exercise of national sovereignty. But neoliberals felt he had offered the best description of the world they wanted to con-serve. Wilhelm Röpke, who taught in Geneva for nearly thirty years, believed that exactly this division would be the basis for a liberal world order. The ideal neoliberal order would maintain the balance between the two global spheres through an enforceable world law, creating a “minimum of constitutional order” and a “separation of the state-public sphere from the private domain.”

In a lecture he delivered at the Academy of International Law at The Hague in 1955, Röpke emphasized the importance of the division while also pointing to its paradox. “To diminish national sovereignty is most emphatically one of the urgent needs of our time,” he argued, but “the excess of sovereignty should be abolished instead of being transferred to a higher political and geographical unit.”

zh: 把民族国家政府放大到整个行星、创建一个全球政府，并非解决之道。新自由主义世纪的难题在于：找到恰当的制度，以维系经济世界与政治世界之间常常紧绷的平衡。现代全球史常被写成从殖民奴役走向民族独立的历程，这类叙事往往轻易略过双重世界对重新想象后帝国世界的影响。很少有思想家比本书所描述的这群经济学家和法学家更深入地探讨过这个双重世界的后果。他们从二十世纪之初就确信，存在且只能存在一个世界经济；他们努力调和经济上的相互依赖与政治上的民族自决。
en: Scaling national government up to the planet, creating a global government, was no solution. The puzzle of the neoliberal century was to find the right institutions to sustain the often strained balance between the economic world and the political world. The consequences of the doubled globe for reimagining the world after empire are dismissed all too easily in narratives of modern global history as the passage from colonial subjugation to national independence. Few thinkers engaged with the consequences of this doubled world more than the group of economists and lawyers described in these pages. Convinced from the beginning of the century that there was and could only be a single world economy, they strove to reconcile mutual economic dependency with political self-determination.

zh: 勒普克在海牙的演讲中提出，解决办法可以在经济学与法律之间的空间里找到。
正如后面的各章所示，日内瓦学派的新自由主义自诞生之日起，与其说是一门经济学的学问，不如说是一门治国术与法律的学问。这些新自由主义者着力最多的，与其说是制造市场，不如说是建立实施市场规则的机构。1962年哈耶克从芝加哥大学转到弗莱堡大学时，便成了德国本土秩序自由主义这一“法律与经济学”传统的继承人；多数学者承认他是弗莱堡学派的盟友，哪怕并不把他视为该学派的一员。
他1960年的著作《自由秩序原理》（
），尤其是他在1970年代所写的三部曲《法律、立法与自由》（
，写于弗莱堡时期），都印证了这一定位，因为他越来越专注于为民主对市场过程的破坏性影响寻找法律与制度上的补救。秩序自由主义者呼吁在民族国家层面制定一部“经济宪法”，日内瓦学派的新自由主义者则与之不同，他们呼吁为整个世界制定一部经济宪法。我认为，我们可以把日内瓦学派的主张理解为秩序自由主义在世界尺度上的重新思考。我们不妨称之为秩序全球主义（ordoglobalism）。
en: In his Hague lecture, Röpke suggested that the solution could be found in the space between economics and law.

As the following chapters show, from its beginnings Geneva School neoliberalism has been less a discipline of economics than a discipline of statecraft and law. More than making markets, these neoliberals have concentrated on making market enforcers. When Hayek moved from the University of Chicago to Freiburg in 1962, he became the heir of the homegrown German law-and-economics tradition of ordoliberalism, and most scholars recognize him as an ally, if not a member, of the Freiburg School.
His 1960 work
and even more so his 1970s trilogy

(written during his time in Freiburg) justify this designation, because he became ever more focused on finding a legal and institutional fix for the disruptive effects of democracy on market processes. Unlike the ordoliberals, who called for an “economic constitution” at the level of the nation, the Geneva School neoliberals called for an economic constitution for the world. I argue that we can understand the proposal of the Geneva School as a rethinking of ordoliberalism at the scale of the world. We might call it ordoglobalism.

zh: 日内瓦学派的新自由主义者提出了一份全球主义蓝图，其基础是多层级治理的制度：这些制度与民主决策相隔绝，肩负着维持统治权的政治世界与所有权的经济世界之间平衡的职责。所有权领域不是自由放任或不干预主义的空间；相反，它是一个需要不断维护、设计和照料，也需要不断通过诉讼加以规整的对象。日内瓦学派想象的核心，是哈耶克在哈布斯堡帝国最先看到的一种愿景——他所称的“双重政府，一个文化的政府和一个经济的政府”的样板。
日内瓦学派的新自由主义者开出的处方，既不是经济对政治的湮灭，也不是国家消解于全球市场，而是两者之间一种精心建构并加以规制的和解安排。
en: Geneva School neoliberals offered a blueprint for globalism based on institutions of multitiered governance that are insulated from democratic decision making and charged with maintaining the balance between the political world of imperium and the economic world of dominium. Dominium is not a space of laissez-faire or noninterventionism but is instead an object of constant maintenance, litigation, design, and care. At the core of the Geneva School imaginary was a vision for what Hayek first saw in the Habsburg Empire—a model of what he called “a double government, a cultural and an economic government.”

Geneva School neoliberals prescribed neither an obliteration of politics by economics nor the dissolution of states into a global marketplace but a carefully structured and regulated settlement between the two.

zh: 如前所述，社会科学家倾向于用“隔绝”这个隐喻来描述新自由主义中国家与市场的关系。这种倾向颇具反讽意味。我们将看到，从1930年代到1970年代，新自由主义者使用的是这个隐喻的地理版本，用来攻击“经济隔绝”之可能性的信念——所谓经济隔绝，是指一定程度的自给自足，可以缓冲全球市场变化给各国带来的冲击。新自由主义者形容，这种对自给自足的执着足以“摧毁普遍社会”“打碎世界”。不过，随着1990年代改用电力隐喻，“隔绝”竟成了新自由主义的一项规范。哈耶克在弗莱堡的一位继任者写道：“哈耶克的主要论点是，他呼吁一种能够有效地把规则制定权威与日常施政的短期要求隔绝开来的制度安排。”

语义的变化是全球经济想象更大转型的一种表征：从以岛屿（insulae）和领土来思考全球经济，转向以一个彼此连通的世界所构成的统一电路来想象它。如今被隔绝的对象，不再是价格信号冲击的最终承受者，而是传递信号的线路本身。然而即便是这个隐喻，终究也不能令人满意。新自由主义的目标比“隔绝”所暗示的缓冲更为绝对。新自由主义者寻求的不是对私人资本权利的部分保护，而是完全的保护，是欧洲法院和世贸组织这类超国家司法机构使可能损及资本在全球享有的权利的国内立法失去效力的能力。因此，我提出以“围封”（
）——而非仅仅“隔绝”世界经济——作为新自由主义规划之想象性终极目标的隐喻——在这个规划中，国家扮演着不可或缺的角色。
en: As noted earlier, social scientists have tended to use the metaphor of insulation to describe the relationship between state and market in neoliberalism. This tendency is ironic. As we will see, neoliberals from the 1930s to the 1970s used a geographic version of the metaphor to attack the belief in the possibility of “economic insulation,” meaning a degree of self-sufficiency that would buffer nations from shocks of change in global markets. Neoliberals described this devotion to self-sufficiency as having the capacity to “destroy the universal society” and “shatter the world.” With the switch to an electricity metaphor in the 1990s, though, it became a neoliberal norm. One of Hayek’s successors at Freiburg wrote, “Hayek’s principal argument is his call for an institutional arrangement that effectively insulates the rule-making authority from the short term demands of day-to-day government.”
The semantic change was symptomatic of a larger transformation of world economic imagination: from thinking of the global economy in terms of islands

and territories to imagining it in terms of a unitary circuitry of a wired world. What is insulated now is not the end target of the shock of the price signal but the wire that transmits it. Yet even this metaphor is ultimately unsatisfying. The neoliberal goal is more absolute than the dampening implied by insulation. What neoliberals seek is not a partial but a complete protection of private capital rights, and the ability of supranational judiciary bodies like the European Court of Justice and the WTO to override national legislation that might disrupt the global rights of capital. For this reason, I propose the metaphor of
rather than mere insulation of the world economy as the imaginary telos of the neoliberal project—a project in which states play an indispensable role.

zh: 这一叙事把新自由主义置于历史之中。它追溯新自由主义全球主义作为一项思想规划：发端于哈布斯堡帝国的灰烬，达于世贸组织创建的高潮。它表明，秩序全球主义是与“民族国家已成为现代世界长期存在的一部分”这一事实共处的方式。新自由主义数十年间所追求的，是为各民族国家的世界提供一种制度性围封，以防统治权与所有权之间的边界发生灾难性的溃决。恰当的制度、法律与有约束力的承诺将保障整体的福祉。这不是一部胜利的叙事——世贸组织的步履维艰，即便往最好里说，对后面各章所描述的那一支特定新自由主义全球主义而言，也不过是一场皮洛士式的胜利。毋宁说，本叙事表明：新自由主义作为一个思想体系，清清楚楚地起源于二十世纪初那场关于如何组织整个地球的危机。
en: This narrative places neoliberalism in history. It traces neoliberal globalism as an intellectual project that began in the ashes of the Habsburg Empire and climaxed in the creation of the WTO. It shows that ordoglobalism was a way of living with the fact that the nation-state had become an enduring fixture of the modern world. What neoliberalism sought over the decades was an institutional encasement for the world of nations that would prevent catastrophic breaches of the boundaries between imperium and dominium. The right institutions, laws, and binding commitments would safeguard the well-being of the whole. This is not a narrative of triumph—the sputtering of the WTO is at best a pyrrhic victory for the specific strain of neoliberal globalism I describe in the following chapters. Instead the narrative shows that neoliberalism as a body of thought clearly originated in an early twentieth-century crisis about how to organize the whole earth.

zh: 是战斗性全球主义，不是市场原教旨主义

整个二十世纪，秩序全球主义深受两个难题的困扰：第一，鉴于民主有毁灭自身的能力，如何依靠民主；第二，鉴于民族主义有“使世界解体”的能力，如何依靠民族国家。第一种张力是研究现代欧洲的学者所熟悉的。众所周知，民主可能产生损害自由的结果，甚至可能经由民主手段导致自我毁灭。许多人——尤其是在德国——相信，两次世界大战之间的经历已经表明民主必须受到限制，必须受到制衡与限制，以防止出现违背自由原则的结果。“战斗性民主”（militant democracy）的观念在1930年代被政治学家发展为理论，并在战后西欧付诸实践。
宪法法院尤其发挥了关键作用，抵御来自左翼和右翼对自由秩序的挑战。许多思想家认同，自由国家必须对那些拒绝宪政秩序的人展现一位社会民主党政客所称的“不宽容的勇气”。
en: Ordoglobalism was haunted by two puzzles across the twentieth century: first, how to rely on democracy, given democracy’s capacity to destroy itself; and second, how to rely on nations, given nationalism’s capacity to “disintegrate the world.” The first tension is familiar to students of modern Europe. It is well known that democracy can have illiberal outcomes and can even lead to its own self-annihilation by democratic means. Many, especially in Germany, believed that the experience of the period between the two world wars had taught that democracy must be limited. It must be subject to checks and restrictions that would prevent illiberal outcomes. The idea of “militant democracy” was theorized by political scientists in the 1930s and put into practice in postwar Western Europe.

Constitutional courts, in particular, played a key role in fending off challenges to the liberal order from left and right. Many thinkers agreed that liberal states must show what one social democratic politician called “the courage of intolerance” toward those who rejected the constitutional order.

zh: 与大众民主的对峙，对新自由主义者而言同样是本世纪的核心。一方面，他们接纳民主，因为民主体供了和平变迁的手段和有利于整个体系的渐进探索空间——这就证明那些把新自由主义者描述为反对民主本身的人是错误的。另一方面，民主孕育着毁灭整体的种子。在反思政治上被动员起来的工人阶级的诉求对自由秩序的挑战时，勒普克在1942年指出：“一个国家可能孕育出自己的蛮族入侵者。”
从美国和英国视角书写的——作为撒切尔政府和里根政府前史书写的——新自由主义运动史，错失了新自由主义关于国内与国际组织的处方所由出的那个特定的后法西斯语境。
事实上，新自由主义者是扬-维尔纳·米勒所称“受约束的民主”（constrained democracy）的关键阐说者。
张力始终存在于两端之间：一端是为和平变迁而倡导民主，另一端是谴责民主颠覆秩序的能力。
en: The confrontation with mass democracy was also at the heart of the century for neoliberals. On the one hand, they embraced democracy for providing a means of peaceful change and a space for evolutionary discovery beneficial to the system at large—thus proving mistaken those who describe neoliberals as opposed to democracy as such. On the other hand, democracy bore the seed of destruction for the totality. Reflecting on the challenges to the liberal order posed by the demands of a politically mobilized working class, Röpke observed in 1942 that “a nation may beget its own barbarian invaders.”

Histories of the neoliberal movement written from the U.S. and British perspectives—as prehistories of the Thatcher and Reagan administrations—miss the specifically post-fascist context of neoliberal prescriptions for domestic and international organization.
In fact, neoliberals were key articulators of what Jan-Werner Müller calls “constrained democracy.”
The tension was always between advocating democracy for peaceful change and condemning its capacity to upend order.

zh: 如果历史学家错过了后法西斯语境，那么他们也错过了后殖民语境。人们很少注意到，哈耶克最初把精力转向重新设计代议制政府，正是回应非殖民化之后“新国家”的出现——用他自己的话说，他选择了一部“制定的”而非“自然生长的”宪法，因而冒着被指前后不一的风险。
他坚持说，他的模范宪法并非为英国而设，而是为“新国家”以及萨拉查治下的葡萄牙这样的法西斯国家而设。谈到新国家，也谈到政治传统“并非完全适用”于民主的南美各国，他写道：“我相信，在世界上这些新近实行民主的地区，限制民主的权力是保存当地民主的唯一机会。如果民主国家不限制自己的权力，它们就会被摧毁。”
历史学家长期忽视这样一个事实：全球帝国的终结，对于新自由主义作为一个知识运动的兴起至关重要。
en: If historians miss the post-fascist context, they miss the postcolonial context too. It is seldom observed that Hayek first turned his efforts toward redesigning representative government—risking the charge of inconsistency by his own confession in adopting a “made” rather than a “grown” constitution—in response to the emergence of “new nations” in the wake of decolonization.

His model constitution was not intended, he insisted, for Britain but for both “new nations” and fascist states such as Salazar’s Portugal. Speaking of new nations as well as countries in South America with political traditions “not entirely adequate” for democracy, he wrote, “I believe that limiting the powers of democracy in these new parts of the world is the only chance of preserving democracy in those parts of the world. If democracies do not limit their own powers, they will be destroyed.”
Historians have chronically overlooked the fact that the end of global empires was essential to the emergence of neoliberalism as an intellectual movement.

zh: 在与大众民主的对峙之外，民族国家与世界之间的相关张力对新自由主义者同样居于核心。民族国家有其用处——它能提供稳定功能（这往往包括对移民的限制），并在政治领域培育合法性。但与民主一样，民族国家也孕育着滑向过界的风险。因此，它必须像民主一样受到约束。新自由主义者信奉一种不妨称为战斗性全球主义的东西，或者借用米勒的术语，称为受约束的民族主义——即需要一套制度保障与法律约束，以防止民族国家违背其对世界经济秩序的承诺。新自由主义者是这样一个制度框架的倡导者：在这个框架中，世界经济能够抵御对其整体完整性的威胁。战斗性全球主义不会取代民族国家，而是与国家协同并通过国家运作，以确保整体的正常运转。
en: Alongside the confrontation with mass democracy, the related tension between the nation and the world was equally as central for neoliberals. The nation could be useful insofar as it provided services of stabilization (which would often include restrictions to migration) and cultivated legitimacy in the political sphere. But like democracy, it also bore the risk of tipping into excess. Thus, it needed to be constrained just as democracy did. Neoliberals believed in what could be called militant globalism or, adapting Müller’s term, constrained nationalism—the need for a set of institutional safeguards and legal constraints to prevent nation-states from transgressing their commitments to the world economic order. Neoliberals were proponents of an institutional framework in which the world economy would survive threats to its holistic integrity. Militant globalism would not displace national states but would work with and through them to ensure the proper functioning of the whole.

zh: 正如后面的各章将会阐明的，把新自由主义者看作国家本身（per se）的批评者是错误的；但把他们看作始终对民族国家抱有疑虑的人则是正确的。1979年哈耶克写道：“在我看来，我们这个世纪建立能够确保和平的国际政府的种种尝试，通常都是从错误的一端接近任务的：创设大量旨在特定管制的专门权力机构，而不是旨在一种真正的国际法——一种能够限制各国政府互相伤害之权力的国际法。”
他把这称为“政治的废黜”，但同样显而易见的是，这是对“民族”的废黜。正如战斗性民主的倡导者看到约束民主的必要，战斗性全球主义的倡导者也看到约束民族国家、并对其主权行使设置限制的必要。
en: As will become clear in the following chapters, it is wrong to see neoliberals as critics of the state per se but correct to see them as perennial skeptics of the
-state. In 1979 Hayek wrote, “It seems to me that in this century our attempts to create an inter

al government capable of assuring peace have generally approached the task from the wrong end: creating large numbers of specialized authorities aiming at particular regulations rather than aiming at a true inter
al law which would limit the powers of
al governments to harm each other.”
He described this as the “dethronement of politics,” but it is just as obviously the dethronement of the
. Just as proponents of militant democracy perceived a need to constrain democracy, proponents of militant globalism perceived a need to constrain
-states and set limits on their exercise of sovereignty.

zh: 战斗性全球主义与赫尔曼·海勒1933年所称的“威权自由主义”（authoritarian liberalism）有相似之处。
与海勒一样，新自由主义者强调：当民众的决定与被视为更高的整体秩序原则相抵触时，就必须能够否决这些决定。学者们已改造海勒的术语来理解欧洲联盟的逻辑。

作为解释性范畴，战斗性全球主义的一个优点在于它关注尺度问题，而许多关于新自由主义思想的论著恰恰忽视了这一点。正如后面的各章所示，对许多新自由主义思想家的处方而言，世界框架并非无关紧要的附带物。他们的愿景也尤其不合于“尺度可变”（dimensions variable）的逻辑。对于关注全球体系性相互依存问题的日内瓦学派成员而言，唯有世界尺度才足够。在他们看来，全球尺度的资本主义是规范性新自由主义秩序不可或缺的前提条件。
en: Militant globalism bears resemblances to what Hermann Heller in 1933 called “authoritarian liberalism.”

Like him, neoliberals emphasized the need to override popular decisions when they controvert what is seen as the superior principle of the order at large. Scholars have adapted Heller’s term to understand the logic of the European Union.

An advantage of militant globalism as an explanatory category is its attention to the question of scale, which is neglected in many treatments of neoliberal thought. As the following chapters show, the world frame was not incidental to the prescriptions of many neoliberal thinkers. Nor was their vision particularly amenable to a logic of “dimensions variable.” For the members of the Geneva School, who were attentive to problems of global systemic interdependence, only the world scale was enough. For them, capitalism at the global scale was the sine qua non of the normative neoliberal order.

zh: 我认为，以战斗性全球主义的精神围封市场，比按照波兰尼式的术语——依市场原教旨主义教义将经济“脱嵌”——来描述，更能道出新自由主义规划的国际维度。波兰尼的观念提供了一个精致的寓言：资本主义世界经济逐步消除自身运行的障碍，直至摧毁其自我再生产的能力。在这个叙事中，市场是贪婪的吞噬者，无情地把土地、劳动力和货币转化为商品，直到社会生活的基础被摧毁。按照这一分析，资本主义需要一个对立面来把自己从自身手中救出来。通过应对并吸纳各种挑战——从工人保险到福利国家——资本主义确保了使其得以存续的社会条件。

正如后面的各章所示，新自由主义规划的一个本质方面，是确定如何通过建造一个能保障资本主义持续存在的超经济框架，先发制人地化解反对力量。新自由主义者构想并为之奋斗的，不是一个自我调节的市场和一个吞噬一切的经济，而是在统治权与所有权之间维持一种持续的和解安排，同时推行政策以加深竞争塑造和引导人类生活的力量。规范意义上的新自由主义世界，不是一个没有国家、没有边界的自由市场，而是一个双重世界——由经济宪法的守护者们把它看管好，使之免于大众对社会正义与再分配平等的诉求。
en: I argue that the encasement of the market in a spirit of militant globalism is a better way of describing the international dimensions of the neoliberal project than the Polanyian terms of disembedding the economy according to a doctrine of market fundamentalism. Polanyi’s ideas provide an elegant parable whereby the capitalist world economy progressively eliminates barriers to its own functioning, to the point that it destroys its own capacity for self-reproduction. In this narrative, the market is omnivorous, relentlessly transforming land, labor, and money into commodities, until the basis for social life has been destroyed. Capitalism, according to this analysis, needs an opposition to save it from itself. By confronting and absorbing challenges, from workers’ insurance to the welfare state, capitalism secures the social conditions that allow it to persist.

As the following chapters show, an essential aspect of the project of neoliberalism was determining how to preempt the opposition by building an extra-economic framework that would secure the continued existence of capitalism. Rather than a self-regulating market and an economy that eats everything, what the neoliberals envisaged and fought for was an ongoing settlement between imperium and dominium while pushing policies to deepen the power of competition to shape and direct human life. The normative neoliberal world is not a borderless market without states but a doubled world kept safe from mass demands for social justice and redistributive equality by the guardians of the economic constitution.

zh: 新自由主义世纪的三次断裂

children: THE THREE RUPTURES OF THE NEOLIBERAL CENTURY

zh: 从新自由主义的视角看二十世纪史，等于给出现代史的一种替代叙述。在新自由主义的世纪史中，非殖民化始于1919年；法西斯主义在竖起关税壁垒之前一度为某些人所看好；冷战从属于对抗“全球新政”的战争；种族隔离的终结在有些人眼中是一场悲剧；国家则只是从属于地球整体性的次级实体。在这个历史里，所谓战后资本主义的黄金时代其实是一个黑暗时代，由凯恩斯主义的迷思和对全球经济平等的错误幻想所支配。它讲述的是一个由货币、信息和货物联结起来的星球的成长历程，而这个世纪标志性的成就，不是国际社会、全球公民社会或民主的深化，而是一个不断一体化的对象——世界经济——以及肩负围封这一经济体系之责的种种制度。
en: A neoliberal perspective on the history of the twentieth century amounts to an alternative account of the modern era. In a neoliberal history of the century, decolonization began in 1919; fascism looked promising to some until it raised tariff walls; the Cold War was secondary to the war against the Global New Deal; the end of apartheid was seen by some as a tragedy; and countries were secondary entities subordinate to the totality of the globe. It is a history where the so-called golden age of postwar capitalism was actually a dark age, governed by Keynesian delusions and misguided fantasies of global economic equality. It is about the development of a planet linked by money, information, and goods where the signature achievement of the century was not an international community, a global civil society, or the deepening of democracy, but an ever-integrating object called the world economy and the institutions designated to encase it.

zh: 后面的各章透过一群新自由主义者的眼睛讲述二十世纪的故事。他们并不认为资本主义与民主相互强化，而是把民主当作一个问题来面对。民主意味着一波又一波叫嚣着提出要求的群众，随时可能把运转中的市场经济掀出轨道。对新自由主义者来说，民主的威胁采取多种形式，从白人工人阶级到非欧洲的正在经历非殖民化的世界。这个世纪以三次断裂为标志，每一次断裂都伴随着德国秩序自由主义者瓦尔特·欧肯1932年所称“世界的民主化”的扩展。
第一次断裂——也是最根本的——是第一次世界大战，各国不再维护世界贸易与投资最重要的条件——金本位制。战后时期造成了政治世界与经济世界之界限的关键性模糊，也就是新自由主义者所称经济领域的“政治化”：随着普选权在西方铺开，中东欧的新国家把追求独立这一正当目标同注定无望的自给自足计划混为一谈，瓦解了旧日的区域分工——而这种分工本身正是世界更大规模相互依存的范本。
en: The following chapters tell the story of the twentieth century through the eyes of neoliberals who did not see capitalism and democracy as mutually reinforcing but who instead faced democracy as a problem. Democracy meant successive waves of clamoring demanding masses, always threatening to push the functioning market economy off its tracks. For neoliberals, the democratic threat took many forms, from the white working class to the non-European decolonizing world. The century was marked by three ruptures, each accompanying an expansion in what German ordoliberal Walter Eucken called in 1932 “the democratization of the world.”

The first, and most foundational, rupture was the First World War, when nations ceased to uphold the most important condition of world trade and investment—the gold standard. The period after the war brought a crucial blurring of the division between the political and economic worlds and what neoliberals called a “politicization” of the economic, as universal suffrage spread across the West and the new nations of East Central Europe mistook the legitimate goal of independence for the hopeless project of self-sufficiency, dissolving the former regional division of labor, which itself modeled a larger interdependence of the world.

zh: 第二次断裂随1929年开始的大萧条而来。1938年之后自称新自由主义者的那些思想家看到，靠学术研究和国际统计专家的协调来恢复失落的世界经济统一是徒劳的。这项任务不仅是根本上政治性的，而且只能是政治性的。众所周知，新自由主义运动的许多领袖人物——包括米塞斯、哈耶克和哈伯勒——的职业生涯始于所谓商业周期研究，即研究经济危机按规律间隔发生的模式。较少为人注意的是，到1930年代末，这一群体已转向，离开了统计学和商业周期研究。我的论点是，他们得出的结论是：世界经济是sublime（崇高）的——超出再现与计量的能力。这一结论使他们从对经济本身的记录与分析，转向设计维持和保护世界经济这一神圣不可侵犯空间所必需的制度。
en: The second rupture came with the Great Depression, beginning in 1929. The thinkers who called themselves neoliberals after 1938 saw the futility of restoring the lost unity of the world economy through academic research and the coordination of international statistical experts. Not
was the task fundamentally political, but it could

be political. It is well known that many of the leading figures of the neoliberal movement, including Mises, Hayek, and Haberler, began their careers as researchers of what was called the business cycle, or the patterns by which economic crises occurred at regular intervals. Less frequently observed is the turn of this group away from statistics and business cycle research by the end of the 1930s. I argue that they concluded that the world economy was sublime, beyond representation and quantification. This conclusion turned them away from the documentation and analysis of the economy as such and toward the design of institutions necessary to sustain and protect the sacrosanct space of the world economy.

zh: 哈耶克在1930年代开始认识到，知识散布于整个市场经济之中，其分散程度之深，使任何个人都永远无法对市场经济如何运作形成整体认识。1930年代的冲击带来了世界经济基本上不可知的觉悟。重建两个世界——众多国家与一个经济——之间关系的任何任务，都只能是一项重新设计国家的工程，并且在1945年之后日益成为一项重新设计法律的工程。这项工程的精髓是多层级治理，即新自由主义联邦主义。在世界经济变得神秘莫测之后，日内瓦学派新自由主义者最有影响力的领域并非经济学本身，而是国际法与国际治理。
en: Hayek began to realize in the 1930s that the dispersal of knowledge throughout an entire market economy was so complete that no individual could ever gain a functional overview of it. The shock of the 1930s brought with it the realization that the world economy was basically unknowable. Any task of reconstructing the relationship between the two worlds—of many nations and one economy—would have to be a project of redesigning the state and, increasingly after 1945, of redesigning the law. The essence of this project was multitiered governance or neoliberal federalism. In the wake of the mystification of the world economy, the Geneva School neoliberals’ most important field of influence was not in economics per se but in international law and international governance.

zh: 本世纪的第三次断裂，与其说是第二次世界大战或冷战带来的——这两者在新自由主义世纪中都鲜有在场——不如说是1970年代全球南方的反叛带来的。1973至1974年的石油冲击把后殖民行动者推上中心舞台。要求经济再分配和经济稳定的强烈诉求，被写入由世界较贫穷国家倡导、联合国大会1974年通过的《国际经济新秩序宣言》。面对全球南方与1970年代借助计算机的全球改造模型的兴起，日内瓦学派发展出自己的愿景：一个没有数字的世界经济——一个信息与规则的世界。对日内瓦学派来说，从1970年代到1990年代的议题，是把世界经济重新思考为一台信息处理器，把全球制度重新思考为这台处理器不可或缺的校准者。贸易规则将通过可在国际上执行的宪法性法律加以实施，以确保稳定。
en: The century’s third rupture came not so much with the Second World War or the Cold War—neither of which have much of a presence in the neoliberal century—but with the revolt of the Global South in the 1970s. The oil shock of 1973–1974 placed postcolonial actors at center stage. Robust demands for economic redistribution and stabilization were enshrined in the Declaration of a New International Economic Order championed by the world’s poorer nations and passed by the UN General Assembly in 1974. Confronting both the Global South and the boom in computer-aided models of global reform in the 1970s, the Geneva School developed their own vision of a world economy without numbers—a world of information and rules. For the Geneva School, the period from the 1970s to the 1990s was about rethinking the world economy as an information processor and global institutions as the necessary calibrators of that processor. Trade rules, enforced through internationally enforceable constitutional laws, would ensure stability.

zh: 日内瓦学派全球主义的兴起，与人们常加给它的所谓自由市场乌托邦主义或市场原教旨主义几乎无关。1930年代的知识分子很清楚：选择项并不是“被治理的民族国家”与“无治理的世界经济”二选一。在我叙述的故事里，一个或许出人意料之处是：发现哈耶克和米塞斯这样通常被描述为自由至上主义者的思想家，竟然就各种形式的国际乃至全球治理的必要性平实而论。在他们看来，民族国家相对影响力的消退，必须伴随超国家机构相应的加强。秩序全球主义的核心，是它自有版本的那个波兰尼所称的市场再嵌入。他与新自由主义者的关键区别在于市场被再嵌入的目的。对波兰尼而言，那是为了恢复人道的分量和社会正义。对新自由主义者而言，那是为了防止国家搞平等主义的再分配，并保障竞争——竞争的另一定义是价格信号系统的最优运转。
en: The rise of Geneva School globalism had little to do with the supposed free-market utopianism or market fundamentalism of which it is often accused. It was clear to the intellectuals of the 1930s that the choice was not between a governed nation and an ungoverned world economy. One of the surprises in the narrative I present may be to find thinkers like Hayek and Mises, who are commonly described as libertarian, speaking matter-of-factly about the need for various forms of international and even global governance. The withering away of the relative influence of national states was always to be accompanied by the corresponding strengthening of supranational institutions. The core of ordoglobalism is its own version of what Polanyi called re-embedding the market. The crucial difference between him and the neoliberals is the ends to which the market is being re-embedded. For Polanyi, it was to restore a measure of humanity and social justice. For neoliberals, it was to prevent state projects of egalitarian redistribution and secure competition, alternatively defined as the optimal functioning of the price-signaling system.

zh: 为一个正在解体的世界提供纵向修复

children: VERTICAL FIXES FOR A DISINTEGRATING WORLD

zh: 二十世纪通常被描绘成新自由主义胜利的时期。这个世纪似乎证明了新自由主义者是对的。除资本主义之外的一切神都失败了。共产主义以戏剧性的瓦解收场。然而，尽管看似已经获胜，整个二十世纪的日内瓦学派新自由主义者却始终被一幅世界正在解体的图景所困扰。他们有时被指责对资本主义的韧性抱有自鸣得意的信心；实际情况恰恰相反，他们忧心的是：支撑资本主义世界经济的全球条件正从根本上受到威胁。在我叙述中心的那些新自由主义者所感受的主导情绪不是狂妄，而是焦虑。他们倾其全力，试图设计出修复方案，以稳定在他们看来岌岌可危的安排。
en: The twentieth century is commonly portrayed as the period of the triumph of neoliberalism. The century had proved neoliberals right, it seemed. All gods other than capitalism had failed. Communism had ended in spectacular dissolution. Despite their apparent victory, however, Geneva School neoliberals throughout the twentieth century were haunted by a vision of a world disintegrating. Sometimes accused of having a smug confidence in the resilience of capitalism, they instead were troubled by the possibility that the global conditions that sustain a capitalist world economy were fundamentally under threat. The dominant emotion felt by the neoliberals at the heart of my narrative was not hubris but anxiety. They expended all of their efforts in attempting to design fixes to stabilize what they saw as a precarious arrangement.

zh: 尽管我关注的只是相对少数的人物，我既不赋予他们超人的力量或因果效力，也不把他们的文本当作圣典。自1980年代以来的时代里，新自由主义思想并未直接映射到现实之上。我不把哈耶克或任何别的思想家的著作当作罗塞塔石碑，用来从必然复杂的现实中辨识出一条内在逻辑。撒切尔和里根获胜以来推行的政策与话语策略，反映着多元的力量与支持群体，必须逐一考察，且难以轻易概括。我也不试图给出关于新自由主义的最后定论，或用一种万能的理论概括数十年来不断变化的全球资本主义。
en: Although I focus on a relatively small number of individuals, I do not ascribe to them a superhuman strength or causality or treat their texts as holy writ. Neoliberal thought has not mapped directly onto reality in the era since the 1980s. I do not nominate the writings of Hayek or any other thinker as a Rosetta Stone for descrying an internal logic to a necessarily complex reality. Policies and rhetorical strategies enacted since the Thatcher and Reagan victories reflect diverse forces and constituencies that must be considered individually and that resist easy general-ization. I do not attempt to deliver either the final word on neoliberalism or a magic bullet theory to summarize decades of ever-morphing global capitalism.

zh: 我转而把日内瓦学派新自由主义者的生平用作穿针引线的线索，串起对一系列制度的讨论——这些制度被设计出来，是为了把全球市场围封起来，免受各国政府的干预。后面的各章提供这些制度的历史实地指南：其中少数制度由新自由主义知识分子首先设计；但对其余的大多数制度，他们扮演的是倡导者、采纳者或改造者的角色。哈耶克“让政治退位”（dethrone politics）的口号，只是新自由主义修复方案的前半部分。后半部分不是让经济登基，而是把经济围封起来，并找到制度形式来执行这一划分。新自由主义者反复寻求一种纵向移动，以解决秩序问题。药方一次次在治理尺度的上移中找到：国际联盟、国际投资法、超国家联邦蓝图、复数票制度体系、欧洲竞争法，以及最终的世贸组织本身。
en: Instead I use the biographies of Geneva School neoliberals as a way to weave through a discussion of a series of institutions that were designed to encase the global market from interference by national governments. The following chapters offer a historical field guide to these institutions, for some of which neoliberal intellectuals were the original architects, but for most of which they played the role of advocate, adopter, or adapter. Hayek’s demand to “dethrone politics” was only the first part of the neoliberal fix. The second was not to enthrone the economy but to encase it and find institutional forms to enforce the division. Neoliberals repeatedly sought solutions to the problem of order in a vertical move. The fix was found, time and again, in a scale shift for governance, including in the League of Nations, international investment law, blueprints for supranational federation, systems of weighted franchise, European competition law, and ultimately the WTO itself.

zh: 新自由主义有时被描述为从某座山巅降临人间——尤其是瑞士的山峰朝圣山（Mont Pèlerin）。新自由主义者自己也乐于营造一种高蹈出尘的印象，频频援引阿列克西·德·托克维尔、伊曼努尔·康德、J. S. 密尔和阿克顿勋爵。然而我们将看到，这些新自由主义名流实际从事的是非常务实的活动——经济知识的运用——他们卷起袖子给企业做顾问、向政府施压、绘制图表、搜集统计资料。整个世纪里，新自由主义者把不同的实体视为世界市场的潜在执行者。下面的叙述始于第一次世界大战刚结束的时期。大战前的全球化话语产出了许多至今仍在回响的母题。经济学家们谈论距离的死亡、边界的过时、自主国内政策的不可能。那个时期还引入了一组构成新自由主义想象之核心的论点。世界经济是统一的整体（

），无法有意义地分割为组成它的各民族国家或帝国。它是相互依存的（interdependent），因为工业国家既依赖外国市场获取原材料，又依赖它们销售产品，供需的波动在全世界都能感受到。它在基础设施上是同质的（infrastructurally homogeneous），包含一个由铁路、电报线路和轮船构成的物质网络，以及法律、金融和生产方面的标准惯例。同时，它在功能上是异质的（functionally heterogeneous），因为不同地区专门从事适合其特定禀赋的经济活动，产生了更大的国际分工，从而更高效地利用世界资源。最重要的是，世界经济拥有一种超国家（
）的力量，能够凌驾于单个政治体影响它的种种尝试之上。
en: Neoliberalism is sometimes described as descending from a mountaintop, the Swiss peak of Mont Pèlerin in particular. Neoliberals themselves promote the impression of a lofty intellectual detachment through their references to Alexis de Tocqueville, Immanuel Kant, J. S. Mill, and Lord Acton. As we will see, though, the neoliberal luminaries were actually involved in very practical activity—the application of economic knowledge—getting their hands dirty in advising business, pressuring governments, drawing up charts, and gathering statistics. Across the century, neoliberals saw different bodies as potential enforcers for the world market. The following narrative begins with the period just after the First World War. Globalization talk before the Great War produced many of the tropes that still echo today. Economists spoke of the death of distance, the obsolescence of borders, the impossibility of autonomous domestic policy. That period also introduced a cluster of arguments that are central to the neoliberal imagination. The world economy was
and could not be divided meaningfully into constituent nations or empires. It was
because industrial nations relied on foreign markets for both raw materials and sales, and fluctuations of supply and demand were felt worldwide. It was infrastructurally homo
comprising a material network of railroads, telegraph lines, and steamships as well as standard conventions of law, finance, and production. At the same time, it was

because different regions specialized in economic activity that suited their particular endowments, producing a greater international division of labor and thus a more efficient use of the world’s resources. Most importantly, the world economy had a
force, capable of overriding attempts by individual polities to influence it.

zh: 国际商会（International Chamber of Commerce，ICC）是一个经济上持有国际主义立场的机构，致力于记录并传播单一世界经济的理念。国际商会汇集国际经济统计，倡导消除贸易壁垒、实现资本自由流动。第一次世界大战结束、哈布斯堡帝国和奥斯曼帝国解体之后，米塞斯和他的圈子觉得它是个不错的伙伴。米塞斯本人就是国际商会的代表，而第一代奥地利新自由主义者都曾在维也纳商会工作。新自由主义学说从一开始就反映了与其商界赞助者需求的交融渗透。第一次世界大战之后出现的“壁垒的世界”（第1章），成为新自由主义者想象其开放世界经济的对位背景。
en: The International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) was an economically internationalist body that sought to document and propagate the idea of a single world economy. The ICC gathered international economic statistics and advocated for the removal of barriers to trade and the free movement of capital. Immediately following the First World War and the dissolution of the Habsburg and Ottoman Empires, Mises and his circle thought it looked like a good partner. Mises himself was a delegate to the ICC, and the first generation of Austrian neoliberals all worked at the Vienna Chamber of Commerce. From the beginning, the doctrine of neoliberalism reflected an intermingling with the needs of its patrons in the business community. The “world of walls” (Chapter 1) that emerged after the First World War became a counterpoint against which neoliberals imagined their open world economy.

zh: 1920年代，国际联盟在某些未来新自由主义者眼中，也像一个超国家权威，或许能够确保资本主义双重世界的条件。米塞斯、哈耶克、哈伯勒和勒普克通过与国联在日内瓦的合作，帮助绘制了最初的综观图景——“数字的世界”（第2章）。但到1930年代末，新自由主义运动的核心部分面对他们所称的经济民族主义——尤其是在中欧——的兴起，索性否认经济能够被看见。哈耶克关于经济无法凭感官把握的立场，与新兴的宏观经济学领域不相一致，但它同时也重新校准了新自由主义的规划：从谈论经济，转向谈论围封经济的框架。
en: In the 1920s the League of Nations also appeared to some of the future neoliberals as a supranational authority that might be capable of ensuring the conditions of capitalism’s doubled world. Mises, Hayek, Haberler, and Röpke helped produce the first synoptic portraits of “a world of numbers” (Chapter 2) in their cooperation with the League in Geneva. By the late 1930s, though, the core of the neoliberal movements responded to the rise of what they called economic nationalism, especially in Central Europe, by denying that the economy could be seen at all. Hayek’s position that the economy could not be apprehended by the senses was inconsistent with the emerging field of macroeconomics, but it also realigned the project of neoliberalism: from talking about the economy to talking about the framework that encased it.

zh: 在1930年代和1940年代，新自由主义者设计了自己大规模秩序的方案，拟定国际联邦的计划，用双重政府的蓝图把不可言说的市场围封起来。罗宾斯、哈耶克和米塞斯提出以“联邦的世界”（第3章）取代帝国。
en: In the 1930s and 1940s, neoliberals devised their own schemes for large-scale order, drawing up plans for international federation in blueprints of double government that would encase the ineffable market. In place of empire, Robbins, Hayek, and Mises proposed “a world of federations” (Chapter 3).

zh: 1944年设计的布雷顿森林体系，很少让新自由主义者看到它能充当世界经济守护者的希望。联合国针对帝国终结开出的药方——给予不断增多的非欧洲国家投票权——威胁着所有权与统治权之间的平衡。新自由主义者再度与国际商会合作，帮助制定了普遍投资守则和双边投资条约，希望借此在“权利的世界”（第4章）中保护资本。
en: The Bretton Woods system devised in 1944 offered scarce hope to neoliberals that it would function as a guardian of the world economy. The United Nations’ solution to the end of empire—granting votes to the proliferating nations of the non-European world—threatened the balance between dominium and imperium. Working again with the ICC, neoliberals helped craft a universal investment code and bilateral investment treaties that they hoped would safeguard capital in “a world of rights” (Chapter 4).

zh: 保卫世界经济的需要，使某些新自由主义者与一些看似背离自由主义的势力结盟。奥古斯托·皮诺切特治下的智利一例臭名昭著；新自由主义与南非种族隔离政权的关系则研究较少。在这里我们会遇到日内瓦学派内部的一次分裂。此处讨论的新自由主义者几乎都拒绝把种族用作分析范畴，1945年之后尤其如此；但威廉·勒普克与众不同，他相信保卫世界经济就是捍卫西方基督教的——也是白人的——原则，抵御另一位新自由主义者威廉·H. 哈特所称的“黑人帝国主义”。
勒普克战后关于“种族的世界”（第5章）的信念，在许多方面都是对日内瓦学派新自由主义主流的一次离经叛道的绕行。哈耶克、弗里德曼和哈特这样的人物也批评国际社会对南部非洲白人少数派政权的外交孤立，但其理由更贴近本书的关切——即不受约束的民主的危险，以及把世界经济秩序与社会正义的政治诉求隔绝开来的必要。
en: The need to defend the world economy led some neoliberals to seemingly illiberal bedfellows. The case of Augusto Pinochet’s Chile is notorious; the neoliberal relationship to apartheid South Africa is less well studied. Here we encounter a split in the Geneva School. Almost all of the neoliberals discussed here rejected race as a category of analysis, especially after 1945, but Wilhelm Röpke is conspicuous for his belief that defending the world economy meant defending Western Christian—and Caucasian—principles against what fellow neoliberal William H. Hutt called “black imperialism.”

Röpke’s postwar belief in “a world of races” (Chapter 5) was in many ways a marked detour from the mainstream of Geneva School neoliberals. Figures such as Hayek, Friedman, and Hutt also criticized the diplomatic isolation of white minority governments in Southern Africa, but for reasons closer to the concerns of this book—namely, the perils of unconstrained democracy and the need to insulate world economic order from the political demands of social justice.

zh: 对日内瓦学派的新自由主义者来说，战后时期最有希望的“经济宪法”执行者，远非南部非洲的种族隔离解决方案，而是欧洲经济共同体（EEC）。1957年随《罗马条约》诞生的，是与基督教民主派、农业利益集团和社会主义者之间的妥协；但一些新自由主义者觉得，它提供了一个潜在模型——一个能够以竞争之名凌驾民族主权之上的“宪法的世界”（第6章）。这个多层级模式看起来像是保障市场权利的一种制度手段。
en: Far more than the segregationist solutions of Southern Africa, the most hopeful enforcer of the economic constitution in the postwar period for Geneva School neoliberals was the European Economic Community. What came into existence with the Treaty of Rome in 1957 was a compromise with Christian democracy, agricultural interests, and socialism, but some neoliberals felt that it offered a potential model for “a world of constitutions” (Chapter 6) that could trump national sovereignty in the name of competition. The multilevel model looked like an institutional means of securing market rights.

zh: 1970年代，日内瓦学派的新自由主义者把欧洲的例子放大，以面对世界较贫穷国家对国际经济新秩序（NIEO）的要求。在哈耶克理论的基础上，他的学生和追随者在关贸总协定内部构建了一套针对国际经济新秩序的反理论，希望阻止他们所称的经济非殖民化从边缘扰乱世界秩序。哈耶克在关贸总协定的学生们发展出这样一种理解：全球经济是“信号的世界”（第7章），用于传达价格；要保存个体经济行动者所依赖的可预期性与稳定性条件，就必须建立具约束力的宪法化法律框架。这一思想是通向世贸组织创建的一股重要知识源流——它是新自由主义在二十世纪为世界经济寻找超经济执行者的规划的一项登峰造极的胜利。
en: In the 1970s, Geneva School neoliberals scaled up the example of Europe to confront the demands of the world’s poorer nations for a New International Economic Order (NIEO). Building on Hayek’s theories, his students and followers at the GATT constructed a counter-theory to the NIEO that they hoped would prevent what they called economic decolonization from disrupting world order from the margins. Hayek’s students at the GATT developed an understanding of the global economy as “a world of signals” (Chapter 7) for communicating prices for which binding constitutionalized legal frameworks were necessary to preserve conditions of predictability and stability for individual economic actors. This thinking was an important intellectual stream leading into the creation of the WTO—a crowning victory of the neoliberal project of finding an extra-economic enforcer for the world economy in the twentieth century.

zh: 1977年，关贸总协定迁入国际劳工组织的前总部，他们把这栋大楼命名为威廉·拉帕德中心，以纪念这位瑞士新自由主义者、首届朝圣山学社会议的东道主——正是他在1930年代和1940年代把勒普克、米塞斯、哈耶克和罗宾斯带到了日内瓦。1995年世贸组织开张时，就在这一栋楼里。日内瓦学派新自由主义这一高点漫长的思想前史表明：新自由主义在其起源处，不仅是一种自由市场的哲学，也是资本主义双重世界中双重政府的蓝图。由于本书的叙述纵贯大半个世纪，它必然是不完整的。它聚焦于1920年代初至1980年代初的时期，大体在里根和撒切尔政府的新自由主义政策突破之前结束。它没有探讨国际货币基金组织和世界银行转向那些后来被称为“华盛顿共识”的政策这一值得研究的题目。同样付之阙如的还有国际货币治理的种种变革，包括货币主义的兴起、布雷顿森林体系的终结、欧元的引入以及中央银行政策的变化。这意味着略去了至为关键的金融问题——那也许是1970年代以来全球资本主义最重要的单项变革。 之所以略去这些问题是，这些题目已由其他作者全面论述，其杰出成果在本导论的注释中有引用。
其他原因则是篇幅的限制，以及我想把一个故事讲得足够细密，以避免困扰社会科学文献那种泛泛之论。
en: When the GATT moved into the former headquarters of the International Labour Organization in 1977, they renamed the building the Centre William Rappard after the Swiss neoliberal and host of the first Mont Pèlerin Society meeting, who brought Röpke, Mises, Hayek, and Robbins to Geneva in the 1930s and 1940s. When the WTO opened in 1995, it was in this building. The long intellectual prehistory of the high point of the Geneva School of neoliberalism shows that, at its origins, neoliberalism was not only a philosophy of free markets but also a blueprint for double government in capitalism’s doubled world. Covering the better part of a century as it does, my account is necessarily incomplete. It focuses on the period from the early 1920s to the early 1980s, mostly ending before the breakthrough of neoliberal policies with the governments of Reagan and Thatcher. It does not explore the worthy topics of the conversion of the IMF and World Bank to the policies that became known as the “Washington Consensus.” Similarly absent are the transformations in international monetary governance, including the rise of monetarism, the end of the Bretton Woods system, the introduction of the euro, and changes in central bank policy. This means leaving out the all-important question of finance, which was perhaps the single most important transformation in global capitalism since the 1970s. One reason for the omission is that these topics have been covered comprehensively by other authors, whose excellent work is cited in this Introduction’s endnotes.
Other reasons are the constraints of space and my desire to tell one story with enough detail to avoid the generalizations that plague the social science literature.

zh: 本书提供的叙事是一个相当有节制的故事，主要通过传记呈现，讲三代思想家：从1920年代维也纳的米塞斯圈，到1980年代协助为世贸组织提供理论建构的日内瓦国际经济律师们。它的焦点是一种特定的双重政府观念——旨在把所有权与统治权各自的领域围封起来的设计。本书在帝国终结之际发生的世界秩序重组中，找到新自由主义全球主义的思想源头，也追溯国际经济法与新自由主义宪政诸范式的历史根源。这些范式过去更多由政治学家和社会学家研究。从日内瓦（而不是芝加哥、华盛顿或伦敦）回望这个世纪，我们看到这样一支思想脉络：它认为世界经济若要存续，就需要限制各民族国家自主性的法律。我们看到的新自由主义版本，其核心价值不是个体的自由，而是整体的相互依存。
en: The narrative offered here is a fairly contained story, presented largely through biography, about three generations of thinkers, from the Mises Circle in 1920s Vienna to the international economic lawyers of Geneva who helped theorize the WTO in the 1980s. Its focus is on the specific notion of a double government form designed to encase the respective fields of dominium and imperium. It finds the intellectual origins of neoliberal globalism in the reordering of the world that came at the end of empire and finds the historical roots of paradigms of international economic law and neoliberal constitutionalism more often covered by political scientists and sociologists than historians. Looking at the century from Geneva (rather than Chicago, Washington, or London), we see a strand of thought that held that, in order to survive, the world economy needed laws that limited the autonomy of nations. We see a version of neoliberalism where the core value is not the freedom of the individual but the interdependence of the whole.

zh: 一开始就应当指出：这里提出的任何观念，从未不受争议地居于统治地位，其中极少有哪种获得过主流常识的地位。新自由主义作为一种历史现象的成败，不能只靠细读其最著名思想家的文本来解释。本书无意论证新自由主义究竟成功还是失败。但我确实打算照亮若干时刻：在新自由主义思想经由与政客、官僚或商人的伙伴关系，被转译为政策或制度设计的那些时刻。作为一个政治规划，新自由主义的许多真实世界效应是有案可查的，人们可以书写它们的历史。本书提供这样一部历史，方法是为新自由主义规划提供一个比其他学者迄今所给的更广阔的框架。现有史著几乎完全忽视的问题——帝国、非殖民化与世界经济——恰恰是新自由主义规划自诞生之日起的核心。日内瓦学派新自由主义的标志性产品——世贸组织——一直被例外、违规和被无视的规则撕裂得千疮百孔，这一事实恰恰说明：经济观念之间的较量远未终结，世界经济仍在被重新界定。
正如一位历史学家所注意到的，关于战后为保护私人产权而建立的那套精密复杂的法律安排，最令人惊讶的事实之一是“它并不管用”。
21世纪初叶的标志，是越来越多的国家拒绝投资条约，或退出既有条约。
越来越多的国家选择不再向国际货币基金组织求贷——以往由强令推行的紧缩计划事后招来选民的惩罚，已使它们学到教训。民族经济主权的种种想象——以及以它之名提出的诉求——已证明是比那些更为乐观的新自由主义理论家所设想的更难啃的硬骨头。
en: It is important to note at the outset that none of the ideas proposed here ever reigned uncontested, and very few had the status of mainstream common sense. The success and failure of neoliberalism as a historical phenomenon cannot be explained only through close study of the writings of its best-known thinkers. I don’t make a case for the success or failure of neoliberalism. But I do aim to shed light on a number of moments where neoliberal thought was translated into policy or institutional design through partnerships with politicians, bureaucrats, or businesspeople. As a political project, the many real-world effects of neoliberalism are documentable. One can write their histories. This book offers one such history by putting the neoliberal project into a broader framework than other scholars have provided to date. All but ignored by existing histories, the questions of empire, decolonization, and the world economy were at the heart of the neoliberal project from its inception. The fact that the paradigmatic product of Geneva School neoliberalism— the WTO—has been riven with exceptions, infractions, and ignored rules only shows that the clash of economic ideas is far from finished and that the world economy continues to be redefined.
As one historian notes, one of the most striking facts about the elaborate legal regime established to protect private property rights in the postwar period is that “it did not work.”
The early twenty-first century has been marked by ever more countries refusing investment treaties or withdrawing from existing ones.

Ever more countries are choosing not to turn to the IMF for loans, chastened by the punishments delivered by electorates after past programs of austerity imposed by diktat. Visions of national economic sovereignty—and claims made in its name—have proven a harder nut to crack than the more optimistic neoliberal theorists believed it would be.

zh: 如今应该比以往任何时候都更清楚的是：讨论新自由主义的秩序观念——尤其是在超国家层面——并不等于断言新自由主义无所不能。自2008年全球金融危机以来，从左翼到右翼的所谓民粹主义运动不断增多，把矛头对准了本书各章所描述的许多制度。在写作本书的这些时间里，全球主义本身也从一个相当冷僻的学术分析用语，变成了右翼口诛笔伐的靶子，助长了赢得这个世界最强权力职位的候选人的竞选气势。全球主义者——如果下定义的话——被想象成金融、政治和学术精英之间一种游移不定、常常面目模糊的组合，习惯性地被当作政治共同体一切病灶的替罪羊，被视为一种危险地脱离了普通人关切之身份幽灵。后面的各章叙述的，正是那些乐于被贴上“全球主义者”标签的人的自我认知。它们有助于把新自由主义拉回地面：不再把新自由主义和全球主义看成抽象的、笼罩历史的整体逻辑，而看成由处于特定时空的具体个人所从事的政治规划。尽管其批评者在扼腕叹息与撰写讣告之间摇摆，其颂扬者在自我夸诩与绝望之间摇摆，新自由主义全球主义依旧是众多论证中的一种。接下来的故事，讲述的不是一场胜利，而是一场持续中的争夺：争夺究竟哪些原则应当主宰世界经济——进而主宰我们所有人的生活。
en: It should be more obvious than ever that to discuss neoliberal ideas of order, especially at the supranational level, is not to assert neoliberal omnipotence. Since the global financial crisis of 2008, so-called populist movements from left to right have multiplied and taken aim at many of the institutions described in these chapters. In the time it took to write these pages, globalism itself has gone from a rather obscure term of academic analysis to a target of right-wing opprobrium, helping to fuel the campaign of the winning candidate for the world’s most powerful office. Globalists, defined (if at all) as a shifting and often shadowy combination of the financial, political, and academic elite, are routinely scapegoated for all that ails the body politic and viewed as specters of an identity dangerously unmoored from the concerns of ordinary people. The following chapters narrate the self-perception of those who would welcome being labeled “globalists.” They help bring neoliberalism down to earth by casting both neoliberalism and globalism less as abstract overarching logics of history than as political projects populated by discrete individuals occupying specific places and moments in time. For all of the alternating handwringing and obituary writing of its critics, and the alternating self-congratulation and despair among its celebrants, neoliberal globalism remains one argument among many. What follows is a story, not of a victory, but of an ongoing struggle to determine which principles should govern the world economy, and, by extension, all of our lives.
